items.excerpt: teams must share unsuccessful results at monthly reviews

codebook.target: Reported normative content in earnings-call accounts: conduct that executives describe as required, encouraged, permitted, discouraged or sanctioned inside the organization, or a routine described as standard practice for a defined set of actors. Calls cannot reveal members' shared beliefs, consensus or norm strength, and the instrument claims none.

categories.name: Collaboration and people-focused
categories.definition: Reported expectations, rules or routines concerning: collaboration, cooperation, teamwork, supportive environment, low levels of conflict, community, communication within the organization, employee well-being, employee equity sharing and compensation, diversity, inclusion, empowerment, or talent development.
categories.indicators: collaboration, teamwork, cross-functional work, supportive environment, psychological safety, internal communication, information sharing, employee well-being, work-life balance, morale, compensation fairness, profit sharing, diversity and inclusion, empowerment, autonomy, voice, talent development, mentoring, learning culture, retention, engagement.
categories.non_qualifying: customers, markets, financial metrics, risk or compliance, or efficiency, unless linked to how people or teams operate internally.

categories.name: Customer-oriented
categories.definition: Reported expectations, rules or routines concerning: sales orientation, customer service, listening to the customer, customer retention, customer experience, customer satisfaction, user experience, client service, being brand-driven, quality of product, quality of service, quality of solution, or taking pride in service.
categories.indicators: customer service, listening to customers, customer feedback loops, retention, customer experience, satisfaction scores used internally, service quality standards, product quality standards, pride in service, brand promise translated into conduct.
categories.non_qualifying: customer demand or market growth reported as outcomes, sales figures, pricing, or competitive positioning without reference to how employees serve customers.

categories.name: Innovation and adaptability
categories.definition: Reported expectations, rules or routines concerning: innovation, creativity, technology adoption, entrepreneurship, adaptability, transformation, flexibility, agility, willingness to experiment, moving beyond tradition, disruption, being fast-moving, quick to take advantage of opportunities, resilience to change, or taking initiative.
categories.indicators: experimentation, pilots, learning from failure, technology adoption as practice, agility in reorganizing work, initiative taking, tolerance for risk in new ideas, speed of decision making, continuous improvement routines, intrapreneurship.
categories.non_qualifying: product launches, R&D spending, or "transformation" programs reported as outcomes or plans without reference to how employees are expected to behave.

categories.name: Integrity and risk management
categories.definition: Reported expectations, rules or routines concerning: integrity, high ethical standards, honesty, transparency, accountability, doing the right thing, fair practices, being trustworthy, risk management, risk control, compliance, discipline, financial prudence, safety, or internal control.
categories.indicators: ethics standards, honesty, transparency with stakeholders, accountability routines, fair dealing, compliance practices (internal or externally required; record origin), risk review routines, safety routines, internal control practices, disciplined capital allocation as a conduct expectation.
categories.non_qualifying: regulatory events, litigation, impairments, leverage ratios or capital returns reported as outcomes without reference to internal conduct expectations.

categories.name: Performance-oriented
categories.definition: Reported expectations, rules or routines concerning: high expectations for performance, achievement, competitiveness, results, hard work, efficiency, productivity, consistency in executing tasks, setting clear goals, following best practices, striving for operational excellence, or exceeding benchmarks.
categories.indicators: performance expectations set for employees, goal setting routines, accountability for targets, productivity practices, operational excellence routines, best-practice adoption, benchmarking of units or teams, incentive links to performance.
categories.non_qualifying: revenue growth, record earnings, margins, guidance or market share reported as outcomes; these are results, not expectations governing conduct.

categories.name: Other reported norms
categories.definition: Reported expectations, rules or routines concerning conduct that does not fit the five categories above. Generic culture declarations without reported conduct are NOT coded here; they are counted in the declaration ledger.
categories.indicators: reported rules or routines about conduct that no specific category covers, e.g. "every manager must hold a weekly one-to-one", when no category indicator applies.
categories.non_qualifying: generic references to "our culture" or "cultural change" without reported conduct (ledger); any item that fits a specific category above; any item with no normative content.

critic_criteria.a: alternative reading under which the conduct is not a normative expectation at all (a one-off decision, an outcome, a plan)
critic_criteria.b: generalizes from an episode to a norm without a stated rule or routine
critic_criteria.c: infers shared culture from a formal rule whose adoption is unobserved
critic_criteria.d: relies on a plan or declaration
critic_criteria.e: scope_type, scope_target or scope_extent wider than the view states
critic_criteria.g: an unresolved source objection undercuts the claim

coding_rules: Record only what the passage states; do not infer motives, rules or norms.
content_type routine only when the passage describes the conduct as standard practice for a defined set of actors; otherwise a reported past action is an episode.
Statements of values or intent with no reported conduct go to the declaration ledger, which never reaches the interpretation stage.
An episode is evidence of at most weak relevance on its own; plans and declarations never establish implemented practice.
Strategy, leadership decisions, financial results and market conditions count only when linked to internal conduct.
A requirement imposed from outside (regulation, customer) is still reported normative content; record its origin as external.
Direction, origin and scope fields are copied from the view and never widened downstream; adjudication may only accept, narrow or withhold.
Unknown or absent information stays unresolved; absence of evidence is insufficiency, not opposition.
Escalate to human review whenever a RESOLVABLE or UNDETERMINED limitation remains or completeness is uncertain.

previous_claims.strongest_objection: The claim may be too broad if sharing unsuccessful results is not specifically about collaboration and people-focused norms.

objections.reason: The claim infers shared culture from a formal rule whose adoption is unobserved. The view states that teams must share unsuccessful results at monthly reviews, but it does not provide evidence that this is a shared normative expectation within the organization.
objections.narrowest_claim: teams must share unsuccessful results at monthly reviews
